title: A stargazer’s view from Kitt Peak
caption: Orion and the Orion-Cygnus Arm of the Milky Way above the Visitor Center observatory, Kitt Peak, Arizona
celestial: Photograph taken at Kitt Peak National Observatory, Arizona
credit: KPNO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/P. Horálek (Institute of Physics in Opava)

recognition.text: NOIRLab Image of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Most pictures of the Milky Way aim at its brightest, densest part, toward Sagittarius. For this one, the photographer turned the other way, toward Orion and its three-star belt, to capture a different stretch of our galaxy: the Orion-Cygnus Arm.

The stars, clusters and nebulae in this arm, such as the red giant Aldebaran at center and the Orion Nebula at center right, have mattered to cultures all over the world, and they are rich places to study how stars live. Our own Solar System lies in this part of the Milky Way.

Below this patch of sky sits the Visitor Center Roll Off Roof Observatory at Kitt Peak National Observatory. While most of Kitt Peak’s telescopes are devoted to research, this one is used only for outreach, so educators and the public can observe the sky from this excellent site.

understand.summary: A ground-based landscape photograph credited to KPNO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/P. Horálek (Institute of Physics in Opava). The source does not publish camera, exposure or color-processing details.
understand.eye: A camera can gather light for longer than the eye, so the Milky Way looks brighter and more detailed here than it would to someone standing on site.
